questions.q: The world's first republic was established at Vaishali by whom?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: Lichchhavi.
questions.source: Eduteria PYQ set — 48th-52th BPSC Preliminary Exam (BH-EDU-058)

questions.q:
Match the following 'World's First' facts with the correct place/person associated with Bihar:
A. World's first democratic republic
B. World's first university
C. World's first prosperous city
D. World's first astronomer 1. Nalanda University 2. Aryabhatta 3. Lichchhavi (Vaishali) 4. Pataliputra
questions.explanation: Lichchhavi (Vaishali) is regarded as the world's first democratic republic, Nalanda as the world's first university, Pataliputra as the world's first prosperous city, and Aryabhatta as the world's first astronomer.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Who was the Temporary (Provisional) Chairman of the Constituent Assembly of India, and who was its Permanent Chairman?

options.A: Temporary - Dr. Sachchidanand Sinha; Permanent - Dr. Rajendra Prasad
options.B: Temporary - Dr. Rajendra Prasad; Permanent - Dr. Sachchidanand Sinha
options.C: Temporary - Dr. Sachchidanand Sinha; Permanent - Mahamaya Prasad Sinha
options.D: Temporary - Satyendra Prasanna Sinha; Permanent - Dr. Rajendra Prasad

questions.answer_text: Temporary - Dr. Sachchidanand Sinha; Permanent - Dr. Rajendra Prasad
questions.explanation: Dr. Sachchidanand Sinha, a Bihari leader, served as the temporary/provisional Chairman of the Constituent Assembly, while Dr. Rajendra Prasad became its permanent Chairman.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Who was the first Indian to hold the post of Governor under British rule (of any province)?
questions.explanation: Satyendra Prasanna Sinha was the first Indian to be appointed as Governor of a province under British rule.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Who was the first Governor of Bihar after India's independence, and in which year did he take office?
questions.explanation: Jairamdas Daulatram became the first Governor of independent Bihar in 1947, while Sir James Sifton (1935) had been the first Governor of Bihar under British rule.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Chief Ministers of Bihar:
1. Mohammad Yunus was the first Chief Minister of Bihar under British rule (1937).
2. Shri Krishna Singh was the first Chief Minister of independent Bihar.
3. Bhola Paswan Shastri was the first Harijan (Dalit) Chief Minister of Bihar.
4. Smt. Rabri Devi was the first woman Chief Minister of Bihar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct: Mohammad Yunus (1937, British-era CM), Shri Krishna Singh (first CM of independent Bihar), Bhola Paswan Shastri (first Harijan CM), and Rabri Devi (first woman CM).
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Who was the first Independent (non-party affiliated) Chief Minister of Bihar, and who was the first Muslim Chief Minister of Bihar?
questions.explanation: Mahamaya Prasad Sinha was Bihar's first Chief Minister not belonging to the Congress party, while Abdul Ghafoor was Bihar's first Muslim Chief Minister.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

options.C: 15 August 1947; Sir Edward Maynard Des Champs Camier

questions.answer_text: 3 February 1916; Sir Edward Maynard Des Champs Camier

questions.q: Who was the first Indian Chief Justice of the Patna High Court, and who was the first Bihari to become Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India?

options.A: Sir Syed Fazal Ali (Patna HC); Bhuvaneshwar Prasad Sinha (Supreme Court)
options.B: Bhuvaneshwar Prasad Sinha (Patna HC); Sir Syed Fazal Ali (Supreme Court)
options.C: Sir Edward Camier (Patna HC); Sir Syed Fazal Ali (Supreme Court)
options.D: Sir Syed Fazal Ali for both

questions.answer_text: Sir Syed Fazal Ali (Patna HC); Bhuvaneshwar Prasad Sinha (Supreme Court)
questions.explanation: Sir Syed Fazal Ali was the first Indian to become Chief Justice of the Patna High Court, while Bhuvaneshwar Prasad Sinha was the first person from Bihar to become Chief Justice of India.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Who was the first Jnanpith Award winner from Bihar, and who was the first Ashok Chakra awardee from Bihar?

options.A: Ramdhari Singh Dinkar (Jnanpith); Randhir Verma (Ashok Chakra)
options.B: Randhir Verma (Jnanpith); Ramdhari Singh Dinkar (Ashok Chakra)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the earliest newspapers of Bihar:
1. Bihar Bandhu (1874) was the first Hindi newspaper of Bihar.
2. The Bihar Herald (1875) was the first English Weekly newspaper of Bihar.
3. The Searchlight (1918) was the first English Daily newspaper of Bihar.
4. Nur-al-Anwar (1876) was the first Urdu newspaper of Bihar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct as per the chronology of Bihar's earliest newspapers: Bihar Bandhu (1874, Hindi), The Bihar Herald (1875, English Weekly), The Searchlight (1918, English Daily), and Nur-al-Anwar (1876, Urdu).
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Where was the first Hindi printing press of Bihar established, and what was it called?
questions.explanation: The first Hindi printing press in Bihar was the Bihar Bandhu Press.

questions.q: Who was the first English traveller to visit Bihar, and in which year?

questions.q:
Consider the following 'largest in Bihar' facts:
1. Largest river of Bihar - Ganga
2. Largest city of Bihar - Patna
3. Largest airport of Bihar - Jayprakash Narayan Airport, Patna
4. Largest railway junction of Bihar - Patna Junction
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct: Ganga is Bihar's largest river, Patna its largest city, Jayprakash Narayan Airport (Patna) its largest airport, and Patna Junction its largest railway junction.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Which railway station in Bihar has the longest railway platform, and which bridge is the largest road bridge of Bihar?

options.A: Sonpur (longest platform); Mahatma Gandhi Setu (largest road bridge)
options.B: Patna Junction (longest platform); Mahatma Gandhi Setu (largest road bridge)
options.C: Sonpur (longest platform); Vikramshila Setu (largest road bridge)
options.D: Mahatma Gandhi Setu (longest platform); Sonpur (largest road bridge)

questions.answer_text: Sonpur (longest platform); Mahatma Gandhi Setu (largest road bridge)
questions.explanation: Sonpur has the longest railway platform in Bihar, while the Mahatma Gandhi Setu (across the Ganga) is the largest road bridge in Bihar.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Which fair is the largest fair of Bihar, and where is it held?
questions.explanation: The Harihar Nath fair, popularly known as Sonpur Mela, is the largest fair of Bihar, held at Sonpur.

questions.q: Which was the first oil refinery of Bihar, and which was the first irrigation project of Bihar?
questions.explanation: Barauni Refinery was Bihar's first oil refinery, and the Son Multipurpose Project was Bihar's first irrigation project.

questions.q: Which was the first planetarium of Bihar, and where is the second planetarium of Bihar located?
questions.explanation: The Indira Gandhi Planetarium in Patna is Bihar's first planetarium, and Darbhanga is home to Bihar's second planetarium.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding universities of Bihar:
1. Patna University (1917) was the first university of modern Bihar.
2. Nalanda Open University was the first open university of Bihar.
3. Magadh University is the largest university of Bihar.
4. Vikramshila University was established by King Dharmapala.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct: Patna University (1917) was the first modern university, Nalanda Open University the first open university, Magadh University the largest university (by affiliated colleges), and Vikramshila University was established by the Pala king Dharmapala.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: Which was the first college of Bihar, and on what date was it established?
questions.explanation: Patna College, established on 9 January 1863, was the first college of Bihar.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content
